notes:
SiriusXM and Spotify play from Sorriva. Both are subscription services with closed catalogues that publish no third-party access; they are reached through the household's own Sonos favorites, which need no developer programme, no API quota, and no authentication by Sorriva at all — the credential lives in the speaker, put there by the Sonos app.

SERVICES ARE A TABLE NOW (migration v24). stations gains serviceId, resMD and householdId; the old source column is gone and its 22 call sites moved with it. Dropping the column rather than leaving it alongside meant the compiler found every reader, including one silently relying on an iHeart default.

A STATION'S IDENTITY IS ITS CHANNEL, not its URI. The same channel saved in two Sonos households carries different account handles in the query string, which the speaker ignores. Matching on the full URI would have put the same station in the library twice.

FOUR PLAYBACK DEFECTS FIXED. DIDL metadata was inserted into the SOAP envelope unescaped — invisible for months because every caller passed an empty string, and the reason SiriusXM would not play. Spotify favorites are containers rather than streams: pointing SetAVTransportURI at one returns 500/714, then Play returns 200 and resumes the previous queue, so they now expand into the queue as local files do. Playback no longer asks iHeart's API about stations that are not iHeart's. The zone picker no longer labels every station 'iHeartRADIO'.

THE LIBRARY SHOWS EVERY SERVICE. Four places read two service names literally, so anything imported through favorites saved correctly and then could not be seen.

TESTS: 74 in the fast suite, under two seconds. Three mutations killed, including the exact escaping bug that shipped. One survived and is recorded as a corrected test rationale rather than quietly re-passed.

NOT IN THIS RELEASE: the service setup screens still differ between services. Redesigned on paper — one screen per service, two panes, tap to add or remove, immediate commit — and logged as fServiceSetupScreens.
